lighting_isotropy.metric: 36-bin land-luminance-gradient peak divided by uniform-bin mean on the delivered source; water-mask pixels excluded and gradients below 12 luminance units excluded
lighting_isotropy.visual_check: No global cast-shadow field, sun angle, sky gradient, or time-of-day lighting was observed. Individual basalt columns still show face-direction brightness differences and bright/dark bevel treatment, so the stricter flat-face-value requirement is not met despite the global isotropy result.

median_conifer_crown_final_scale.measurement: Median visual crown width across 20 isolated ordinary conifers distributed over the source, scaled by 2560/1254. An automated dark-green component threshold under-segmented branch tips and returned 17 source px / 34.70 final px / 1.67 m; that lower result is retained here as corroborating evidence that scale is below the required range, not as the primary visual measurement.

buildable_vs_steep_fraction.basis: manual estimated fraction of non-water land area
buildable_vs_steep_fraction.method: Coherent high moor and rim shelves count as buildable; exposed chasm walls, the fall wall, and near-vertical drops count as steep; dense conifer ground, talus, floating fragments, and broken rim terrain make up the remainder.

water_mask.encoding: opaque white water pixels on fully transparent non-water pixels; binary alpha
water_mask.derivation: Full wet-pixel extents manually traced from the source raster around the side stream, fall, spray, luminous pool, visible cascade, south-east tarn, and tarn spill; filled surface extents rather than centerlines; low-saturation mist excluded.

source_scale_gate_proxy.note: The repository Node runner is not exposed in this managed shell. The local proxy also classifies nearby cyan-leaning conifer and crystal pixels as fringe, so its failure is not proof that those non-water pixels should be added to the mask; owner or pipeline review remains required.

authority_conflict.claim_a: The required edit target's authored neighbour paint stays in place and the stitch preserves neighbour pixels.
authority_conflict.claim_b: No painted water may touch the east source edge; only the south-east tarn contact on the south edge is allowed.
authority_conflict.evidence: The supplied edit target already contains the south-east tarn reaching the east side of the source window. The delivered raster and complete all-water mask therefore contain 90 wet east-edge pixels and 18 wet south-edge pixels.
authority_conflict.ruling: The no-east-water rule remains the validation authority, so the candidate is reported noncompliant on the east edge. Omitting those wet pixels from the mask would violate the all-painted-water rule and create a false coastline.

open_risks: Basalt columns retain bright/dark face and bevel variation rather than one flat value per face; the global key-light metric does not establish compliance with the stricter column-shading rule.
The preserved south-east tarn context reaches the east source edge and is correctly included in the all-water mask, conflicting with the literal no-east-water rule.
Median conifer crowns measure 49.0 px / 2.35 m at final canvas scale, materially below the required 84-147 px / 4-7 m range.
Visual inspection finds more than twelve violet crystal clusters, although they remain confined to chasm rims and floating fragments.
The local 6 px and 48 px water-fringe proxies fail; their detector visibly includes nearby conifer and crystal pixels, and the official Node gate could not be run in this shell.
The chasm-floor stream is mostly obscured by low-saturation mist; only distinctly painted wet pixels were masked, because mist over water is explicitly excluded.

South-band haze continuity, exact rock drum continuity at the stitch boundary, face-value flatness, crystal count, fantasy register, and overall terrain quality remain owner visual decisions; mechanical checks do not establish visual acceptance.
